lines.t: London built a brand new bridge. Two days later, they had to close it. And nothing was broken.
It was a thin steel blade over the river. Three hundred and twenty-five meters. Just for walking.
On opening day, ninety thousand people came to cross it.
And halfway across... the bridge started to sway. Left. Right. Left.
People grabbed the rails. Some froze. Some laughed.
Engineers checked everything. The steel was fine. The wind was weak. The bolts were tight.
They shut it down. And the whole city gave it a new name. The Wobbly Bridge.
So they tested it with real people. A small crowd? Nothing.
A bigger crowd... and suddenly, it swings.
You see, when the floor slides under your feet, you don't fight it. You spread your legs and sway, like walking on a boat.
Now picture thousands of people doing that at the same time. In step. Every step pushes the bridge further, and that makes even more people sway along.
Fixing it took almost two years, and five million pounds of giant shock absorbers.
Then the engineers marched seven hundred of their own staff across it. Not a wobble.
So the bridge was never the problem. The crowd was.
Would you have crossed on day one? A, yes. Or B, no way.
